entities.summary:
Acron, son of Zeno of Elea, was a Greek physician born at Agrigentum in Magna Graecia.

He is known for his work on the theory of the four causes and his contributions to the development of medicine during the Classical period.

Acron's most notable achievement was the discovery of an antidote for poison, which he documented in his book 'De Veneno'.

His work had a lasting impact on the field of medicine, influencing future generations of physicians, including Galen and Hippocrates.

Acron's legacy extends beyond his medical contributions, as his writings also explored the relationship between philosophy and medicine.

The discovery of an antidote for poison by Acron stands out in history as a testament to human ingenuity and perseverance.
